title: POC scoping — prompt storage, redaction & benchmark sizing (HorizonPay)
summary: Initial POC scoping for HorizonPay: align on success criteria, define workload shape for benchmark, decide prompt storage and redaction approach, retention policy options, and pilot timeline. Customer prefers hosted for speed but needs VPC/KMS option if regulated. Agreed to run token-level benchmark (100k monthly -> 10 qps average, 40 qps peak) and redaction test on synthetic PII. Next steps: Redwood to share benchmark plan, security FAQ, and a cost sketch; HorizonPay to share sample prompts and compliance checklist.
next_steps: Redwood: send benchmark plan and cost sketch (by 2025-11-12)
HorizonPay: share 20 representative prompt examples + traffic histogram (by 2025-11-10)
Schedule 90-min technical deep dive for redaction implementation (tentative 2025-11-17)
Agree on pilot success metrics and sign SOW to start dedicated pilot if needed
action_items: Sophie Nguyen: Prepare benchmark plan (tokens, qps, latency targets) due 2025-11-12
Diego Moreno: Draft redaction/obfuscation options doc with implementation notes due 2025-11-14
Arun Iyer: Provide sample prompt file and histograms due 2025-11-10
Leah Ortiz: Send compliance checklist and required SOC2 artifacts link by 2025-11-11
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Karla (Redwood SE), Maya (CTO), Arun (Lead ML), Leah (Security), Ben (Infra)

[00:00] Sophie: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick off. is this time good for folks?
[00:09] Maya: yeah good thanks, we got 45ish minutes, hope that works.
[00:12] Sophie: great. quick agenda: align on success criteria for the poc, workload sizing for benchmarks, and talk through prompt storage / redaction and retention. Diego will cover the technical approach and options.
[00:25] Diego: hey all. to set expectations, we typically run a small benchmark phase: synthetic traffic that mirrors your histograms, plus a redaction test on a sample corpus. we want to validate latency, cost, and quality regression.
[00:37] Arun: quick context — HorizonPay uses LLMs for payment assistant flows and KYC summarization. Production is about 100k tokens/month today in experimental stage, but we expect spikes up to 40 qps during business hours for campaign peaks. latency under 400ms P50 is ideal.
[00:51] Sophie: perfect, that helps. what's the current infra? cloud native? VPC?
[00:56] Ben: we're on AWS, VPC enabled, S3 for artifacts, internal KMS for keys. For the pilot we prefer hosted for fast start but must be able to switch to VPC/private if compliance requires.
[01:08] Leah: and SOC2 is mandatory for our vendors; we also have strict retention rules — default prompts with PII must be purged after 30 days unless redacted and approved.
[01:20] Diego: okay so two main constraints: short retention window + redaction. Options are: 1) no prompt storage (ephemeral only) for PII flows, 2) store prompts encrypted with customer KMS but disable plain-text logs, 3) store minimal prompts and hash keys for audit. each has tradeoffs for debugging and replay.
[01:37] Maya: we need the ability to replay the exact prompt for debugging within that 30-day window, but only if redaction/PII removed. otherwise it must not be accessible.
[01:46] Sophie: that maps to our feature flags — we can flip prompt_storage: off for the PII route, and enable customer-kms-backed storage for sanitized flows.
[01:56] Diego: note — our runtime supports prefix caching (kv cache) and continuous batching which impacts concurrency; if you disable prompt storage entirely, some cache hit rates might drop and cost per-token rises.
[02:08] Arun: can you quantify that? i.e., cost delta if we disable storage for PII-heavy paths?
[02:12] Diego: rough rule: with cache/prefix enabled you can see 15–30% token cost reduction on chat-style flows. disabling storage or not using caching could move you towards the higher end. we'll quantify in the benchmark.
[02:26] Ben: also curious about dedicated capacity — if we go dedicated, is retention handled differently?
[02:31] Karla: dedicated gives you isolated pools; you still pick storage policies. private deployment (VPC/on-prem) gives you full control over logs and persistence, which solves most compliance asks but takes longer to provision.
[02:45] Leah: timeline question: how long to get private deployed for pilot?
[02:49] Sophie: private setup usually takes 6–8 weeks after agreement; dedicated is faster — reserved pools in 1–2 weeks with some lead time. Hosted pilot we can start this week with simulated data if you want.
[03:03] Maya: we'd like to start hosted for speed but ensure we can do a quick switch to VPC or dedicated if compliance flags it. is that supported?
[03:11] Diego: yes — we support routing policies and fallbacks. you can start on hosted, and if you need a VPC we can do model pinning and deployment to private within the timeline I mentioned, though rolling state like KV cache won't migrate automatically.
[03:26] Arun: for the benchmark itself, what do you need from us? tokens, qps, sample prompts?
[03:30] Diego: sample prompts with typical lengths, a traffic histogram for qps peaks and p50/p95 latency targets, and a list of success metrics. we'll run a 3-day baseline with your sample traffic, a redaction test, and a stress run for peak traffic.
[03:42] Sophie: suggested success criteria (proposed): p50 < 400ms, p95 < 1200ms, pass quality metric of >0.95 on our reranking/acceptance test, and redaction false negative rate <1% on synthetic PII set.
[03:58] Leah: that redaction FN <1% is critical. how do you do redaction now?
[04:02] Diego: options: client-side redaction before sending, server-side on ingestion with an automated PII model, or a hybrid where sensitive fields are replaced with tokens and a secure mapping stored under customer KMS. each option has different latency and audit tradeoffs.
[04:18] Maya: we prefer server-side if we can show auditable logs that do not include raw PII. but we also need a way to redact in the replay for debugging.
[04:27] Diego: that's the hybrid approach — store tokens mapped to redacted values in an encrypted store. access is governed by RBAC and requires explicit approval in the audit trail.
[04:36] Ben: what about prompt storage for embeddings or rerank? do embeddings store raw text?
[04:41] Karla: embeddings we can either not persist or store encrypted; many customers store only hashes + metadata to avoid raw text retention. for rerank you usually need the candidate set — we can store candidates encrypted or obfuscated.
[04:54] Arun: for telemetry and troubleshooting we need some logs. can you provide redacted traces?
[04:59] Diego: yes we can offer token-level cost and lat breakdowns and sanitized traces that replace PII with placeholders. full traces are available if stored under customer KMS in a private deployment.
[05:11] Sophie: i'll note the differences: hosted = fastest, limited KMS integration for prompt storage (we do bring-your-own-key for some tiers), dedicated = reserved capacity + stronger isolation, private = full control.
[05:24] Maya: cost sketch? ballpark for 100k tokens/month baseline and peak test at 40 qps?
[05:30] Sophie: we gave a rough number on the last email but we'll send a concise cost sketch with benchmarking scenarios. roughly, hosted inference unit costs are lower for small volumes; dedicated unit cost improves at higher sustained throughput but has commit. we'll put concrete numbers in the follow-up.
[05:44] Arun: for success criteria on the POC: 1) functional parity on summary generation, 2) latency targets met under 90% of normal traffic, 3) redaction FN <1% on synthetic data, 4) clearly defined rollback/fallback plan if performance degrades.
[05:59] Diego: noted. we'll build the benchmark to capture those.
[06:03] Leah: about retention: our policy is 30 days for raw prompts, 1 year for audit hashes only. can you enforce per-route retention?
[06:11] Karla: yes we have per-route retention policies; you can set shorter retention for PII routes. we also support on-demand purge APIs.
[06:20] Maya: how about alerts for drift/regression in redaction quality?
[06:24] Diego: Redwood Optimize can hook into evaluation sets and send regression alerts tied to prompt sets. we can set thresholds and alert on day-over-day drifts.
[06:33] Ben: provisioning question — for the demo/pilot, what's the minimal work to get data flows in?
[06:38] Sophie: minimal: create an API key, route a subset of traffic to Redwood endpoint, and supply sample prompts. for redaction test, send synthetic PII corpus. we can do all that on hosted.
[06:49] Arun: are we able to toggle prompt_storage via header or route config?
[06:53] Diego: yes, route-config flags or SDK headers can set prompts_to_store=none|encrypted|minimal. also a masking header for live redaction.
[07:03] Maya: regarding logs and audits — Leah will need to see proof of encryption at rest and KMS integration. can you send SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration doc?
[07:12] Sophie: yes we'll include SOC2 summary and KMS integration notes in the follow-up.
[07:17] Leah: also include details about RBAC and SSO (SAML) support.
[07:21] Karla: we support SAML SSO and fine-grained roles. we'll include sample RBAC policies.
[07:29] Diego: technical note on benchmarks — we'll run three phases: baseline (normal qps), redaction accuracy test (synthetic PII), peak stress test. expected runtime ~48 hours total but we can parallelize.
[07:43] Arun: sounds good. i'd like the benchmark to include 95th percentile latency for short prompts (<=64 tokens) and long prompts (>=512 tokens).
[07:52] Diego: will do. we'll also include tokenization variance and model variant comparisons (int8 quantized vs fp16) if you want to evaluate cost vs quality.
[08:03] Maya: yes include quantization impact. important for cost decisions.
[08:07] Sophie: recap — action items and next steps (see follow-up). Any final questions?
[08:13] Maya: none here. thanks.
[08:16] Leah: one quick: do you have a recommended redaction model?
[08:20] Diego: we typically use a small PII model for pre-ingest filtering, combined with pattern rules. we'll include recommended model sizes and sample precision/recall numbers.
[08:29] Sophie: ok we'll send the plan. thanks everyone.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors present; some proper nouns may be misrecognized (e.g., KMS vs K M S, Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as "Redwood Dedic8ed").

End of transcript.
